The fan-shaped SRR absorber can achieve a 10 dB fractional bandwidth of 4.5%, which is about 4 times wider than the 1% bandwidth of the conventional rectangular SRR absorber.
The fan-shaped SRR absorber has a second absorption band at 11.7 GHz with over 20 dB reflection coefficient and an 8% fractional bandwidth.
The modified HIGP absorber has a 10 dB bandwidth from 9.5 GHz to 10.5 GHz, which is almost double the 5.5% bandwidth of the conventional HIGP absorber.
The modified HIGP absorber achieves a minimum reflection coefficient of over 20 dB at the center frequency, compared to only around 12 dB for the conventional HIGP design.
Both the fan-shaped SRR and modified HIGP absorbers can maintain their performance for both co-polarized and cross-polarized incident waves.
The metamaterial absorbers reported in this paper have a very thin physical thickness of only 1.6 mm.
The fan-shaped SRR absorber can increase the bandwidth by up to 8 times compared to the conventional rectangular SRR design.
The modified HIGP absorber has almost double the 10 dB fractional bandwidth compared to the conventional HIGP absorber.
Electromagnetic full-wave simulations were used to calculate the reflection coefficients of the proposed metamaterial absorbers.
The proposed metamaterial absorbers were designed and simulated for operation in the X-band frequency range.
The fan-shaped SRR and modified HIGP absorbers were fabricated on an FR4 substrate with relative permittivity of 4.4 and loss tangent of 0.02.
Surface mount resistors of 375 Ohms were used to connect the patches in the modified HIGP absorber design.
The fan-shaped SRR geometry was proposed to enhance the parasitic effects and achieve wider/multi-band absorption.
The modified HIGP absorber design involved cutting asymmetric rectangular slots in the patch elements.
The goal of the new metamaterial absorber designs was to improve the absorption level, bandwidth, and polarization performance compared to conventional designs.
